Keywords: Solidus coins and supplies in kind
RagShortTexts: The solidus weighed about 4.5 g; armies also relied on grain and transport supplied in kind.

Variants.Content: The solidus was an imperial gold coin of high fineness, with a standard weight of about 4.5 grams, used for substantial payments, gifts and accounting. Money and actual army provisions were distinct: provinces also supplied grain, fodder and transport, with some obligations commuted into money under prescribed arrangements. Assessments, collection methods and delivery points shaped the burden.

A soldier receiving gold still needed someone selling food; on campaign, rations and transport remained essential. Merchants receiving substantial gold payments checked weight and appearance, while small transactions also used silver, copper or barter. A full purse did not ensure fodder along the road.

Military finance required accounts of both money and provisions. Stored grain needed carriers, and coins had to reach their recipients. Arrears, commutation and changed delivery points could burden a locality; authorizing expenditure did not mean the army had received its supplies.
